demo.title: Asking is not the same as being allowed.
demo.intro: An illustration that runs in your browser and is connected to nothing. Start the request and watch where it stops. It will not go any further until you approve that exact revision yourself.
demo.approvalLabel: Your approval covers only the target, operation and revision shown above.
demo.halt: Stopped here. The flow is waiting for a human decision and will not continue on its own.
demo.legend: Refused · Waiting for a person · Passed
demo.initial: DENIED · production/payment-api sits outside staging/*, and nobody has approved it.
demo.denied: DENIED · This action is outside the standing scope, or it no longer matches the approval on file. It stops here for a person to look at.
demo.approved: APPROVED · Your approval is bound to the target, operation and revision shown, so the request clears the gate and the flow runs to the end. Nothing real was touched.
demo.allowed: ALLOWED · This exact request now has authority, so the flow runs to the end. Nothing real was touched.
demo.invalidated: APPROVAL REVOKED · The request changed, so the previous approval is void — even if you set the values back to what they were.
demo.evidence: Illustrative evidence: identity workflow-agent-17, the target and revision, the policy decision, and what the approval actually covered. After a real action you still compare what happened against what was approved, and reconcile any difference.
demo.static: A restart of production/payment-api by workflow-agent-17, which is authorized only for staging/*, is refused. A human approval naming that target, the restart operation and revision 182 permits that one request and nothing else. Identity and permissions come from the execution layer, never from what the model claims about itself.

home.eyebrow: FACTOR IO / KUBERNETES · INFRASTRUCTURE · ENTERPRISE AI
home.headline: The complete private AI bundle, from bare metal to local inference.
home.lede: We don't sell third-party cloud API wrappers. Factor IO engineers the complete on-premise bundle: bare-metal Kubernetes, authoritative knowledge systems, and private local AI running entirely within your enterprise boundary—delivered directly by a principal architect.

sections.title: The full bundle is the deliverable, not an isolated model.
sections.body: Enterprise AI cannot survive in production without the platform underneath it and data authority around it. Selling a model or technique in isolation invites project failure. Factor IO delivers the whole architecture as an integrated bundle: bare-metal GPU clusters, knowledge authority mapping, private local model serving, and mechanical execution controls.

sections.title: Engineered for local security, air-gapped systems and compliance.
sections.body: When sensitive corporate data cannot leave your network or be billed on unpredictable API tokens, local on-premise AI is the only viable architecture. We address the hard operational questions before installation begins:

items.title: Where does the model run?
items.body: Strictly on your private servers or local Kubernetes clusters—using optimized local runtimes (vLLM, Triton, Ollama) with zero outbound data leakage.

items.title: Which document is authoritative?
items.body: Source authority and document lifecycle are settled before indexing, preventing hallucinated answers from obsolete company policies.

items.title: Who is permitted to see what?
items.body: Retrieval filters enforce existing active directory and RBAC permissions mechanically at query time, not by prompting the model.

items.title: What happens when hardware fails?
items.body: High availability, failover domains, and automated recovery are engineered into the Kubernetes cluster from Day 1.

sections.title: The platform first, the data foundation, then sovereign AI.
sections.body: Every layer reinforces the others. You can engage us for the complete turnkey rollout or a specific phase aligned with your roadmap.

items.title: Kubernetes & GPU Platform
items.body: The platform your applications need, including Kubernetes and GPU infrastructure. It is designed to carry whatever the business runs on it rather than one workload in particular. Capacity, recovery, upgrades and day-to-day ownership are part of the design.

items.title: Private Local AI Implementation
items.body: On-premise inference engines, model quantization, local embeddings, and GPU capacity optimization with predictable, zero-token cost and total data sovereignty.

items.title: Knowledge and Authority Mapping
items.body: Make your organisation's information useful to AI: which sources to trust, who can access them, and how to keep them current before algorithmic indexing.

items.title: AI Governance and Controls
items.body: Decide what AI may do on its own and when a person needs to approve the next step. We design controls around those decisions, including access, review and deterministic refusal.

sections.title: Transparent engagement scopes. Direct engineering quotation.
sections.body: Because every enterprise environment has distinct security constraints, hardware baselines, and data policies, we don't sell generic price-tag commodities. We scope directly with you and deliver a transparent quotation within 48 hours.

sections.body: Four clear stages with defined deliverables, agreed before anything gets built.

items.body: Review your goals, existing systems and constraints. Identify what needs attention first and define the quotation scope.

items.title: 3. Build & Local AI Pilot

items.title: 4. Deploy & Hand Over
items.body: Prepare the operating procedures and work through them with your team. Agree any ongoing support separately.

sections.body: Each service can be a standalone engagement or a phase of the complete bundle delivery. The platform work comes first because everything else sits on it. We agree technical scope and provide an itemized quotation before implementation begins.

items.title: Mechanical AI Governance
items.body: Decide what AI may do on its own and when a person needs to approve the next step. We design controls around those decisions, including access, review and deterministic refusal.

sections.title: An instruction is a request. A permission is a fact.
sections.body: This is what the AI governance service produces: a decision made before the action runs, not a rule written into a prompt and hoped for. The illustration below is the shape of that control, not a product you buy.

sections.title: Send people the cases that genuinely need a person.
sections.body: AI handles the volume; people handle the judgment. What gets escalated is written down as a rule during design, so nobody is asked to trust a confidence score without seeing the evidence behind it.

items.title: Normal result
items.body: Runs under the policy already approved.

items.title: High-value transaction
items.body: Always goes to a person.

items.title: Missing evidence or conflicting data
items.body: Stops and asks someone accountable.

items.title: Low confidence
items.body: Escalates instead of guessing.

items.title: Against policy
items.body: Blocked, then routed to review.

items.title: Wide blast radius
items.body: Needs explicit approval first.

sections.title: Keep model choice separate from authority.
sections.body: Agents can run on local, enterprise-hosted or frontier models. Identity, authorization, scope, approval, tool access, state, audit and reconciliation are checked before any of them reach your systems. Choosing a different model does not change who is allowed to do what.

sections.title: AI workflows need maintenance, not just a launch.
sections.body: Review the corrections people made, the outputs they rejected, the escalations and exceptions, how long things take and what changed in the data and the business rules. AI can propose improvements, but every change is tested, reviewed and released as a controlled revision. Production policy never changes quietly. Ongoing support is agreed separately, per project.
